action: Long-press the middle of the price pane for ~900ms
response: A CROSSHAIR appears: dashed vertical and horizontal lines at the touch point, a price badge '723.62' on the price scale, a date badge 'Tue 07 Jul 26' on the time axis, the legend switches to full OHLC ('O 750.22 H 750.96 L 745.21 C 747.71 -3.57 (-0.48%)' and 'Vol 43.72 M'), and a PLUS BUTTON renders immediately to the left of the price badge.
result: ⭐⭐ LONG-PRESS IS THE CROSSHAIR, AND IT CARRIES A QUICK-ACTION PLUS BUTTON
url: self-captured V2, iPhone 17 Pro / iOS 26.6, landscape
notes: ⭐⭐ RESOLVES THREE INFERRED ROWS WITH ONE GESTURE - CHART-0018 (long-press), ALERT-0003 (the price-scale plus button) and ALERT-0004 (long-press a price level enables the quick-alert entry point). It is also the cleanest statement of TradingView's touch philosophy: a phone has no hover, so LONG-PRESS IS HOVER, and the app spends that gesture on the single richest read - full OHLCV plus the exact date plus the exact price - and then attaches an action affordance to it.

target: Plus button beside the crosshair price
action: Tap the plus button next to the crosshair price badge
response: A FIVE-ITEM PRICE-LEVEL ACTION MENU opens, every item pre-filled with 723.62: 'Add alert on SPY at 723.62' | 'Buy 1 SPY @ 723.62 limit' | 'Sell 1 SPY @ 723.62 stop' | 'Add order on SPY at 723.62...' | 'Draw horizontal line at 723.62'
result: ⭐⭐ A PRICE LEVEL IS ITSELF AN OBJECT WITH A UNIFORM, PRE-FILLED ACTION VOCABULARY
notes: ⭐⭐ THE STRONGEST SINGLE PIECE OF EVIDENCE FOR PRIMITIVE P2 IN THE ENTIRE TEARDOWN, and it EXTENDS P2 beyond what the V1 census claimed. P2 was 'price series, indicators and drawings share one action vocabulary'. This shows the abstraction goes further: an ARBITRARY PRICE THE USER POINTED AT is also an object, with alert / buy / sell / order / draw, all pre-filled. ⭐ Item five is the quiet masterstroke - 'Draw horizontal line at 723.62' promotes a crosshair READING into a DRAWING, which is TradingView's answer to touch imprecision from the opposite direction to P1: you do not need an accurate finger if you can turn an accurate readout into an object.

target: Alert creation from the price-level menu
action: Tap 'Add alert on SPY at 723.62', then open the alerts manager to verify
response: NO dialog, no form, no confirmation. The alerts manager immediately listed 'SPY Crossing 723.62 - SPY - Active'.
result: ⭐⭐ AN ALERT AT AN ARBITRARY CHART LEVEL IS THREE GESTURES AND ZERO TYPING
url: self-captured V2; alert created then deleted in the same minute
notes: ⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE PARITY METRIC, NOW SETTLED BY MEASUREMENT ON BOTH SIDES. TradingView: long-press (1) + plus (2) + Add alert (3) = an active Crossing alert at a level the user chose by eye, with no keyboard. UCT: More tools (1) + Set price alert (2) + TYPE THE PRICE + Alert above/below (3). The gesture counts are equal; the difference is that TradingView never asks for a number because the chart already knows which number you meant. ⛔ This also CORRECTS the V1 estimate of '2 taps' for the price-scale route - it is 3, because the plus opens a menu rather than committing. Recording the correction rather than keeping the flattering number.

action: Long-press an alert row in the manager
response: A NATIVE iOS context menu (blurred backdrop, the row lifted and highlighted) with five items: Stop | Edit | Clone | Delete (red) | Open Chart. Choosing Delete raised a second native alert: 'Delete alert and its logs? Doing this will permanently delete SPY alert and all its logs.' with Cancel / Delete.
result: ALERT ROWS CARRY A NATIVE iOS CONTEXT MENU AND A CONFIRMED DELETE
notes: NEW ROW. ⭐ AND IT REVEALS A COHERENT PRINCIPLE the app follows consistently: DESTRUCTIVE ACTIONS ON SERVER-SIDE OBJECTS ARE CONFIRMED WITH A NATIVE iOS ALERT (exiting bar replay, deleting an alert, deleting a layout - all three observed), while destructive actions on LAYOUT-LOCAL objects are not (deleting a drawing is silent, UNDO-0005). That is not sloppiness, it is a deliberate line drawn at 'can undo recover this'. Worth adopting as a rule rather than case-by-case.

action: Tap the price scale, then tap the revealed 'L' badge
response: Tapping the price scale REVEALED two small badges at its foot - 'A' (filled, active) and 'L' (unfilled). Tapping 'L' filled it and re-rendered the price scale with logarithmic spacing (780 / 760 / 740 / 700 / 680 unevenly spaced), and the crosshair price re-mapped from 723.62 to 721.62. A and L are INDEPENDENT toggles - both can be lit at once.
result: ⭐ LOG SCALE IS TWO GESTURES, AND AUTO/LOG ARE INDEPENDENT TOGGLES NOT A RADIO GROUP
portrait: CHART-0026 verified the same disclosure in portrait on iPhone 15 / iOS 17.5
notes: ⭐ CONFIRMS CHART-0026's 'Visible on tap' on a SECOND device and OS, and resolves CHART-0023. ⚠️ IMPORTANT HONESTY CORRECTION TO THE UCT COMPARISON: the revealed badges measure roughly 20 points square - so they are ALSO well under the 44pt minimum. TradingView's advantage over UCT's permanently-visible 17x11 toggles is therefore NOT that its targets are bigger; it is that they cost ZERO pixels until asked for. ⛔ Do not write the recommendation as 'make the toggles bigger like TradingView' - TradingView's are small too. Write it as 'hide them until the scale is tapped', which is the actual finding.

action: Tap the trash on a layout row (the disposable research layout, which was also the ACTIVE layout)
response: A confirmation dialog: 'Delete this chart layout? Doing this will permanently delete your "UCT MOBILE RESEARCH - DELETE ME" layout with all drawings.' with Cancel and a red Delete. On confirm the layout was removed and the app fell back to the NEXT layout in the list, opening it without modifying it (its timestamp was unchanged).
result: ⭐ DELETING A LAYOUT IS CONFIRMED, NAMES THE LAYOUT, AND WARNS ABOUT DRAWINGS
notes: UPGRADED FROM INFERRED, and it settles the concern raised in LAYOUT-0004 about an always-visible trash on every row of a scrolling phone list. The affordance IS guarded, the copy is specific (it names the layout and says 'with all drawings'), and deleting the ACTIVE layout degrades gracefully to the next one WITHOUT dirtying it. That is the well-behaved version of a dangerous control.

action: Attempt to enable BrowserStack's Screen Reader control on this device
response: 'Screen Reader (Beta) - Screen Reader is currently not supported for this device.'
result: ACCESS_LIMITED ON THIS DEVICE - VoiceOver could not be exercised
notes: ⚠️ RECORDED HONESTLY RATHER THAN INFERRED. The A11Y area stays at or near zero and the reason is now specific rather than vague: BrowserStack's Screen Reader is device-gated and this device is not on the supported list. A different device in the fleet may support it, which is a concrete V2 action rather than an open question. ⛔ Do NOT infer TradingView's VoiceOver behaviour from the fact that the chart is a canvas - a canvas can carry a full accessibility tree, and asserting otherwise without testing is exactly the kind of claim this census refuses to make.
